newsitem.title: USA: USDA to trim wheat sowings forecast-head economist.
newsitem.headline: USDA to trim wheat sowings forecast-head economist.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department will lower its projection for wheat sowings, but corn and soybeans will be "about the same" as suggested earlier this month, the department's chief economist said Wednesday.
Overall, economist Keith Collins told Reuters there would be no major changes in the projections for acreage and output but price projections might change.

The projection for wheat sowings would drop, he said, while corn and soybeans would be roughly the same. Soybeans might be up "a little." In the case of corn and soybeans, he said, figures would change by one million acres or less.

When the administration's proposed fiscal 1998 budget was released earlier this month, it projected 81.5 million acres of corn, 64 million of soybeans, 72 million of wheat and 13.8 million of cotton. Projections were based on November conditions.
Updated figures will be released at USDA's Outlook Forum next week.
"There's not a lot of reason to change them very much," Collins said. "I don't expect much of a change."
The drop in winter wheat sowings, documented in January, would prompt a reduction in the overall U.S. wheat figure.

Farmers sowed 48.2 million acres of winter wheat, down three million from a year earlier and the lowest amount since 1978. Collins said wheat export figures also might be lowered because of signs that China has abundant supplies of wheat and will import less.

Projections issued earlier this month by two groups suggested corn plantings of 80.7 million acres, soybeans at 64 to 65.1 million acres, wheat at 70.2 to 72.8 million acres and cotton at 13.15 to 13.86 million acres.

The Congressional Budget Office has projected 79.8 million acres of corn, 73.5 million of wheat, 65.2 million of soybeans and 13.5 million of cotton. CBO figures were based on December conditions and updated figures were to be issued soon.

Two analysts said USDA probably would not make major changes to its projections. One analyst said USDA traditionally makes incremental change and the other said "not a whole lot of new information...comes along" during late winter.
In the projections that accompanied the budget, USDA pegged likely corn output at 9.6 billion bushels, soybeans at 2.4 billion bushels and wheat at 2.3 billion bushels.
The Food and Agricultural Policy Research Institute has projected corn at 9.49 billion bushels, soybeans at 2.44 billion, wheat at 2.39 billion and cotton at 18 million bales.
The U.S. Feed Grains Council has projected corn at 9.49 billion bushels, soybeans at 2.38 billion bushels, wheat at 2.45 billion bushels and cotton at 17.4 million bales.
